title: Did you see it? Stunning photos of Northern Lights that painted Island's skies pink
excerpt: The Northern Lights lit up Isle of Wight skies on Saturday, October 10, with predominantly pink Aurora Borealis visible across the Island.
content:
Jon Moreno

Sat, 31 October 2026 at 8:16 pm UTC

ISLANDERS were treated to a spectacular celestial show over the weekend as the Northern Lights illuminated skies across the Isle of Wight.

Shades of pink could be seen stretching across the night sky, as the Aurora Borealis put on a dazzling display, visible from several parts of the Island on Saturday night (October 10).

County Press readers captured the enchanting phenomenon on camera, sending in a host of striking photographs.

The Northern Lights, more commonly seen near the Arctic Circle and in northern parts of Scotland, were visible much further south thanks to heightened solar activity.

The colourful display continued into the early hours of yesterday (Sunday), creating memorable scenes for stargazers and photographers alike.

Experts say the rare spectacle was caused by charged particles from the Sun interacting with Earth's atmosphere, producing the shimmering colours associated with the Aurora Borealis.

The Met Office has said sightings could remain possible during periods of clear skies until tomorrow (Tuesday), offering skywatchers another chance to catch a glimpse of the natural phenomenon.

Many residents took to social media to share their excitement, with some describing the sight as "amazing" and "stunning".

The County Press would like to thank everyone who submitted photographs for our gallery.
